(i) the "morphing technique" is a useful tool for fitting ab initio potentials to spectroscopic data and (ii) the 4-mode potential representation appears to be adequate for the chloride-water system.

the n-mode representation, with n=3-4, is converged to within 5-10 cm-1 of the exact result for the fundamental frequencies and that this representation is suitable for fitting intermolecular potential surfaces to spectroscopic data.

the "morphing technique" provides an effective way of fitting intermolecule interaction potentials to measured vibrations, and that a 4-mode coupling expansion of the interaction potential for Cl-(H2)O is sufficient to reproduce the experimental frequencies to within 10-15 cm-1.
